laws.rule: Mount Rinjani National Park climbing tickets for foreign visitors, from 3 November 2025: IDR 250,000 per day (about A$19.56, RBA rate of 30 October 2026) on the Sembalun, Senaru and Torean routes and IDR 200,000 (about A$15.65) on Aikberik, Tetebatu and Timbanuh.

local-law.note: Route openings change with fire and weather closures; check the park before booking.

layers.authority: Balai Taman Nasional Gunung Rinjani (national park office, Ministry of Forestry)
layers.process: Climbing Mount Rinjani needs an e-ticket booked through the park's eRinjani app. The park announced that from 1 September 2026 the park is open only in a limited way (climbing, ritual, religious, cultural, social and research activity) because of fire risk, with tighter patrols and bag checks, and that online booking through eRinjani is paused from 1 September 2026 until fire risk is declared safe. Bookings made and paid before that date can still be served. Check the park's notices before planning.

The Torean climbing route was closed from 23 September 2026 until further notice after a fire at Bukit Setampol. Ticket holders for Torean are asked to reschedule or switch to another entry or exit route; climbers already on the mountain can be redirected out through Sembalun or Senaru on rangers' direction.

On the three Gili islands (Meno, Air and Trawangan) the regency regulates passenger transport by non-motorised vehicles: cidomo (horse carts), cikar and hire bicycles. It sets caps per island (for example Gili Trawangan: up to 50 cidomo, 65 cikar and 3,225 bicycles; Gili Air: 25, 25 and 1,500; Gili Meno: 20, 20 and 750) and requires owners to register each vehicle and renew a registration every year. The regulation is about the non-motorised fleet; it is not a published statement of a motor vehicle ban.

sources.title: Peraturan Bupati Lombok Utara 4/2024 (second amendment to Perbup 27/2011, Gili Matra non-motorised transport)
